question: Which of the following rules determines the direction of the magnetic field produced by a current carrying circular loop?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right-Hand Thumb rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right-Hand Thumb rule**, also known as **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**, is the fundamental principle used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** associated with a **current-carrying conductor**, including a **circular loop**.
 
• According to this rule, if you imagine holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your **right hand** such that the **thumb points** in the direction of the **current**, then your **fingers** will wrap around the conductor in the direction of the **field lines** of the magnetic field.
 
• When applied to a **circular loop**, every section of the wire generates magnetic field lines in the form of **concentric circles**. By applying the **Right-Hand Thumb rule** to any segment of the loop, one can see that the field lines inside the loop all point in the **same direction**.
 
• At the **center of the circular loop**, these magnetic field lines appear as **straight lines**. The strength of the magnetic field produced is directly proportional to the **amount of current** flowing through the loop and the **number of turns** in the coil.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field depends on the direction of the current; if the current flows in a **clockwise direction**, the magnetic field enters the face of the loop (acting as a **South Pole**), and if it flows **anticlockwise**, the field emerges from it (acting as a **North Pole**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is primarily used to find the direction of the **magnetic force** acting on a moving charge or a current-carrying wire placed in an external magnetic field.
 
• It is the working principle behind **electric motors**.
 
• The **thumb** represents the direction of the **force (motion)**, the **forefinger** represents the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** represents the **current**.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a magnetic field.
 
• It is the fundamental principle for **electric generators**.
 
• The **thumb** points in the direction of the **motion of the conductor**, the **forefinger** in the direction of the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** indicates the direction of the **induced current**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field of a Solenoid:**
 
 
• A **solenoid** is a long coil containing a large number of close turns of insulated copper wire.
 
• The magnetic field produced by a solenoid is similar to that of a **bar magnet**, with one end behaving as a **magnetic North pole** and the other as a **magnetic South pole**.
 
• The **Right-Hand Thumb rule** is also used here to visualize the field lines looping through the center of the coil.
 
 
 
• **SI Units and Constants:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density) is the **Tesla (T)**.
 
• The magnetic effect of current was first discovered by **H.C. Oersted** in **1820**, proving the link between **electricity and magnetism**.
